summary: Phase 149O.3 -- HATP Hardware Provider Independent Verification (Wave 5): verification-only independent audit of Phase 149O.2's Wave-5 hardware-provider surface. Reconstructed the exact Wave-5 production diff from the 149O.1J baseline 89bebdc0 (exactly four files, UNRELATED hunks = 0) and re-derived Wave-5's requirement ownership (HATP-REQ-016..025, HATP-REQ-076) from the 149O.1D plan's own text rather than from 149O.2's report. Added tests/test_phase_149o_3_hatp_hardware_provider_independent_verification.py (242 passed, 1 hardware-required skip), methodologically independent by rebuilding every WebAuthn structure from raw bytes and raw JSON instead of calling the production module's own helpers, then proving byte-equality with the fido2 library. Independently probed hardware: zero FIDO2 and zero PIV devices attached, so hardware key storage, key non-exportability and physical touch are classified as provider-semantic or requires-real-hardware, never as verified. Attacked payload byte-exactness, a fourteen-dimension replay matrix, user-presence derivation and replay, the new protected hardware-credential registry's trust root, the trust conjunction with the Wave-2 store, software and test credential exclusion, the production provider factory's closed allowlist, evidence-schema strictness, optional-dependency behaviour, and the Wave-4 operational-readiness hard ceiling. Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- HATP WAVE 5 HARDWARE PROVIDER CONFORMS, with zero Blocking findings. Thirteen findings recorded and none repaired, of which three are non-blocking defects (B-149O.3-1 credential-registry readiness omits three Wave-2 ownership checks; B-149O.3-3 registry schema version declared but never validated; B-149O.3-8 provider verify() raises for twelve structurally-malformed-evidence inputs instead of failing closed, contained by Wave 4's exception wrapper) and ten are observations. Two prior-phase characterisations were independently corrected: the ninety-one-failure HATP baseline is root-caused to Python interpreter version rather than timezone, which also resolves the RAE count discrepancy 149O.2 declined to investigate; and the full suite is unrunnable under pytest-xdist because of a pre-existing collection-time uuid4 parametrization in 149O.1H, proven pre-existing by stashing this phase's changes. Fast Green 4652 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed at exact baseline. HATP-001 v1.0 byte-identical by hash, zero production files changed, zero dependency change. HATP PRODUCTION: NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: Wave 6 -- RAE Integration.

validation_results.name: fido2_protocol_reconstruction_and_payload_binding
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 re-derived the signed-bytes construction from the installed fido2 1.2.0 source in two independently agreeing places (ctap2/base.py:153 public_key.verify(self.auth_data + client_param, self.signature); server.py:428 cred.public_key.verify(auth_data + client_data.hash, signature)). Full chain: challenge = SHA-256(canonical_payload); clientDataJSON base64url-embeds it; signed bytes = authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON). Both hashes intentional and contract-conformant (HATP-REQ-076 freezes no algorithm; HATP-REQ-020 demands demonstration, which was done). This phase's fixtures rebuild every WebAuthn structure from raw bytes and raw JSON, never calling the production _payload_digest/_serialize_evidence helpers, then prove byte-equality with the library -- so a helper-level error could not cancel out. VERDICT: HARDWARE PROVIDER PAYLOAD BINDING: EXACTLY DERIVED FROM VERIFIED WAVE-3 CANONICAL SEMANTICS.

validation_results.name: byte_exact_payload_and_replay_matrix
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 exercised all 14 signed semantic dimensions with real ECDSA signatures over real Wave-3 canonical payloads: payload byte (5 offsets), truncation, extension, repository, decision_record_id, decision_record_digest, binding_id, binding_digest, operation AG3 job_id, operation AG3 commit, operation AG5, timestamp, provider profile, principal, credential. validation_results.name: hardware_credential_registry_trust_root_attacks
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 attacked the new protected registry independently. Production root is a fixed platform path (/Library/Application Support/PCAE/HATP/hardware-credentials on macOS, /etc/pcae/hatp/hardware-credentials on Linux), never inside repository state. Non-redirectable by 10 environment variables (HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, TMPDIR, PWD, PCAE_HATP_CREDENTIAL_ROOT, HATP_CREDENTIAL_STORE, PCAE_HOME, PCAE_CONFIG), by CWD, by CLI flag, or by constructor/production() argument (production() takes zero parameters; positional injection raises TypeError). Unsupported platform fails closed for win32/cygwin/aix/freebsd12 and non-POSIX os.name. Root pre-creation attack attempted for real: /Library/Application Support is drwxr-xr-x root:admin and os.access(parent, W_OK) is False, so the agent principal provably cannot create the authority root. Symlinked root and symlinked artifact both refused. Duplicate JSON keys, duplicate credential IDs, and 11 malformed-document variants all fail closed. Missing registry returns None, never a trust grant. No auto-provisioning: after lookup and environment_status the root is still empty and a missing root is never created. Read-only API: public surface is exactly {production, root, environment_status, lookup_credential}; no enroll/grant/authorize/rotate/revoke/write/create/save/update/delete; executable source has no write_text/write_bytes/mkdir/os.remove/unlink/rename/chmod/open(. VERDICT: HARDWARE CREDENTIAL REGISTRY: PROTECTED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY VERIFIED.

validation_results.name: trust_conjunction_and_cross_deployment_replay
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 verified the two protected stores are complementary and neither is independently sufficient. The Wave-5 credential registry carries no repository_id, canonical_deployment_root, or principal_id (identity/authority is Wave-2 only) and Wave-2 SignerRecord carries no key material (cryptography is Wave-5 only). verify_hatp_proof requires lookup_signer, lookup_principal, lookup_authority AND resolve_deployment_authorization in addition to the provider outcome. Exercised end-to-end with the real FIDO2 provider: the same authentic credential and the same real signature yield VALID at the bound deployment and WRONG_DEPLOYMENT at a relocated one. Proof self-selection is structurally impossible -- HumanApprovalProvenanceProof has no public_key/certificate/attestation/cose_key field (HATP-REQ-077 upheld at the type level); an attacker key against an empty registry yields signature_valid=False.

validation_results.name: software_and_test_credential_production_exclusion
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 confirmed no software or test credential can enter the production path. There is no production write API into the credential registry at all, so a software key cannot be enrolled through PCAE. A production-constructed Fido2HardwareProvider resolves the fixed protected root, which does not exist on this machine, so an authentic software-key assertion through that path returns signature_valid=False. Production factory rejects 14 hostile profile strings including TEST_PROVIDER_V1, SOFTWARE, CUSTOM, ../../../evil, fido2, FIDO2, HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_V1-extra, case variants, whitespace variants, empty and PIV; the allowlist is exactly one element. create_production_hardware_provider never returns TestHATPProofVerifierProvider (type-checked and AST-checked with docstrings stripped). No production module outside hatp_providers.py references TestHATPProofVerifierProvider or _fake_assertion, and inside it the only executable occurrence is the class definition line. PIV fallback requires explicit allow_piv_fallback=True, default False. VERDICT: PRODUCTION PROVIDER FACTORY: CLOSED, TEST/SOFTWARE PROVIDERS EXCLUDED.

validation_results.name: evidence_schema_and_cryptography_strictness
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 attacked the evidence envelope and the cryptographic path. Correct fail-closed behavior confirmed for unknown field, missing field (all 5), duplicate JSON key, 8 unknown version values, invalid UTF-8, non-object evidence, credential mismatch, provider-profile mismatch, wrong client-data type (4 variants), wrong challenge, wrong origin (4 variants), wrong RP-ID hash (3 variants), tampered signature, 4 malformed-DER mutations, signature from a different key, registry public-key substitution, public-key type confusion (RSA/Ed25519/P-384), and malformed COSE material. Signature verification is delegated to the library's COSE implementation with no custom ECDSA math. Only UP is treated as security-bearing; UV/AT/ED/BE/BS are not consulted. Origin and RP-ID hash are genuinely enforced predicates, not decorative fields. Two new findings recorded and NOT repaired: B-149O.3-8 (NON-BLOCKING) and B-149O.3-9 (OBSERVATION) -- see their own entries.

validation_results.name: finding_b_149o3_8_verify_raises_instead_of_failing_closed
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 FINDING B-149O.3-8 (NON-BLOCKING, new, NOT repaired): Fido2HardwareProvider.verify() raises for structurally malformed evidence, violating the frozen HATPProofVerifierProvider.verify contract text 'MUST NOT raise for an invalid/unrecognized assertion -- return signature_valid=False instead'. Root cause: _parse_fido2_evidence performs bytes.fromhex(), AuthenticatorData(...) and CollectedClientData(...) outside the HATPFido2EvidenceMalformedError boundary while verify() catches only that one type. Reproduced for 12 inputs: non-hex and odd-length signature_hex, non-hex credential_id_hex/authenticator_data_hex/client_data_json_hex, truncated/empty/36-byte authenticator data (ValueError); non-JSON and empty clientDataJSON (JSONDecodeError); clientDataJSON missing challenge (KeyError). This narrows the scope of 149O.2's own evidence_format_strictness claim that malformed evidence never raises -- that claim holds only for the five envelope-level cases it exercised. Scoped precisely: signature_hex='' IS handled correctly. Contained: verify_hatp_proof wraps the provider call in except Exception and maps it to INVALID_SIGNATURE, verified end-to-end, so HATP still fails closed in every case. The defect is confined to the provider layer's own reusability contract.

validation_results.name: attestation_contract_disposition
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 re-derived the attestation disposition from HATP-001 directly and explicitly NOT from HATPProviderVerificationOutcome.attestation_valid being Optional. HATP-REQ-019 enumerates the HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_V1 properties as exactly (a)-(e) with no (f) and with the word attestation absent entirely; HATP-REQ-023 uses MAY; HATP-REQ-024/025 constrain attestation rather than mandate it; HATP-REQ-079 says 'attestation valid where required'. Mechanically confirmed that no sentence in the 979-line contract pairs 'attestation' with a positive SHALL -- every attestation SHALL is a SHALL NOT. Implementation is honest: device_attestation=False, conformance downgraded to CONFORMANT_WITH_NON_BLOCKING_LIMITATIONS, no attestation_object/AttestationObject/attStmt/verify_attestation/x5c handling, no production code ever sets attestation_valid=True (AST-verified: every occurrence is the constant None), and no attestation_root symbol exists anywhere in src/pcae/ so Root 2A is not claimed proven. Wave-4 behavior None->VALID and False->INVALID_ATTESTATION is contract-correct for this profile. DISPOSITION A: ATTESTATION NOT REQUIRED FOR WAVE-5 PROVIDER CONFORMANCE -- contract explicitly defers it.

validation_results.name: piv_fallback_disposition
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 confirmed PIV is DEFERRED/UNAVAILABLE and that deferral is permitted. Re-derived from the plan's own conditional stop condition: PIV is triggered only if the FIDO2 spike cannot bind HATP's canonical payload as the signed challenge. This phase independently demonstrated that the FIDO2 binding does work, so the trigger never fired and the contract/plan does not require both provider profiles to exist. The placeholder never fabricates success: imports only pcae.core.hatp_providers (no pkcs11/pyscard/smartcard), capabilities() reports NOT_CONFORMANT with every property False, credential_identity() and request_signature() raise unconditionally, verify() returns signature_valid=False unconditionally, and the source contains no signature_valid=True or human_presence_proven=True. No weak PIV fallback can be silently instantiated.

validation_results.name: hardware_backed_key_and_non_exportability_disposition
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 independently determined what the hardware-backed-key claim actually rests on. A software EC P-256 key proves protocol correctness, signature verification, payload binding and credential binding, but proves nothing about hardware key generation, hardware storage, or non-exportability. Legitimate bases for non-exportability would be: authenticator-generated credential, CTAP2 protocol semantics, FIDO certification, or device attestation -- the last of which is NOT implemented this phase, so per-device certification is unavailable. The implementation rests on CTAP2 semantics and says so, and its capability note also carries an explicit 'REAL HARDWARE NOT EXERCISED in this development environment' disclaimer, with the conformance verdict deliberately downgraded. 'PCAE does not expose an export API' is explicitly NOT accepted as proof; it was verified only as necessary hygiene (no private_key/private_bytes/PrivateKey/export_key symbol on either side; request_signature accepts no key parameter). 149O.2 did not overclaim. VERDICT: HARDWARE-BACKED KEY PROPERTY: ARCHITECTURALLY SUPPORTED BUT NOT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED.

validation_results.name: security_property_evidence_classification_a_b_c
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 classified every Wave-5 security property into the three mandatory categories without collapsing B/C into 'verified'. Category A (proven by software test): canonical-payload/challenge binding, byte-exactness, the full 14-dimension replay matrix, credential/public-key binding, key-type confusion rejection, origin and RP-ID-hash enforcement, evidence-envelope strictness, UP derivation and non-caching and non-transferability, absence of caller-supplied presence, the entire credential-registry protected-root discipline, production-factory closure and test-provider unreachability, optional-dependency behavior, the operational hard ceiling, and the integration-boundary absence. Category B (provider/API-semantic, not physically exercised): fresh physical presence per signing operation, HATP-REQ-018's physical half, cancellation/timeout and device-fault mapping, multi-device selection. Category C (requires real hardware, currently unverified): hardware key generation, key non-exportability in fact, credential hardware provenance, live request_signature, and HATP-001 section 44 attacks #6 and #20 in hardware-in-the-loop form.

validation_results.name: finding_b_149o3_10_ninety_one_failure_baseline_root_caused
validation_results.result: Phase 149O.3 FINDING B-149O.3-10 (OBSERVATION, pre-existing, Wave-3, out of scope, NOT repaired): the 91-failure combined-HATP baseline is interpreter-version-dependent, not 'environment/timezone-dependent' as 149O.2 characterised it. _parse_iso_timestamp delegates to datetime.fromisoformat, whose accepted lexical set widened in Python 3.11. Demonstrated directly: 2026-01-01T12:00:00Z, ...123+0000, ...,123Z and ...123+01 all raise ValueError on CPython 3.9.6 and are accepted on CPython 3.14.5. Consequently the identical selection gives 91 failed under 3.9.6 and 0 failed under 3.14.5. This also resolves the RAE 16-failed-vs-4-failed discrepancy 149O.2 explicitly declined to investigate -- same cause. It matters because pyproject declares requires-python = '>=3.9', so under the project's own declared minimum interpreter HATP's accepted timestamp lexical set is narrower than the Wave-3 tests assert. Unrelated to Wave 5 and unaffected by the fido2/cryptography installation, which touches no timestamp code. Recommended disposition: a dedicated Wave-3 timestamp-portability phase.
